categories.name: Quick guide
categories.content:
Open help with F1 or the main-menu button. Select a page and a category. Mods selects an active mod document.

Left-click an object for details; hold right-click for a preview. Titles and hover hints show native IDs. Ban markers use current restrictions.

Press Sort or a filter to choose a value. Gold frames highlight dropdown rows under the pointer. Level selectors can be combined; All levels clears them. ID is the default order and Reset restores it. Later explicit sort choices, filters and the selected mod are remembered when reopening or resizing.

Type an object, category or hotkey title in Search. Ctrl+F focuses it. Choose a scope; click a result or use Up/Down and Enter. Native results reveal and highlight an object. Right-click previews a result. Clear or Escape returns to browsing. Article bodies are not searched.

Hotkeys combines active sources and groups bindings by context. A mod has its own hotkey category when documented. These lists describe bindings; they do not register keys.

categories.name: Object catalogues
categories.content:
Creatures: town, neutral, war-machine and commander categories; levels 1-7; movement and attack filters. Cards show live statistics, cost, growth, abilities and upgrades. Only creatures with a nonempty name and combat DEF name are listed. Town icons appear only on faction categories.

Artifacts: class categories, equipment position and combination filters. Cards show effects, cost and combination components. Only artifacts with a nonempty name, description and a visibly nonempty artifact.def frame are listed. IDs 144 and 145 are inventory placeholders and are always excluded. There is no artifact level filter.

Heroes: town categories and sorting, including might/magic groups. Cards show portraits, specialties and starting data; left-click also shows the biography.

Spells: school categories, levels 0-5, Use and Damage filters. Multi-school spells can appear in several categories. All 81 native spells include creature abilities 70-80, grouped at level 0. Mastery tables show mana, effect and Spell Power formulas.

Secondary skills: groups and all three mastery descriptions for 28 skills.

Towns: names, rosters and hero classes from the game. Available through global Search and integration calls.

objects.value: Click a button to open a card or a library tool. These examples use built-in resources and need no extra script.
Native DEF images: creature #0 uses portrait frame 2; artifact #7 uses frame 7.

categories.name: Writing mod help
categories.content:
Place a JSON file in an active mod's lang directory. Its root is help.<actual lower-case folder>. name is a display name and may differ from the folder key. Copy examples/help_authoring.json and replace its my mod key to start.

categories contains article records with name and content. hotkeys has a section name and numeric records containing keys, name, description and type. Metadata only documents bindings. Contexts: EVERYWHERE, ADV_MAP, HERO, TOWN, COMBAT, MAIN_MENU and OTHER. Missing contexts become Other.

Categories accept arrays or numeric-key objects; use a numeric-key object with name for hotkeys. Keep indices consecutive. Reading stops after 32 missing records or index 4095. A usable hotkey list generates runtime category 0; article indices then shift by one.

An optional description appends Overview. Plugins is appended only for actual .era, .dll and .bin files in EraPlugins, EraPlugins/BeforeWog or EraPlugins/AfterWog. It lists supplied files, not load status. Optional plugins records contain file, name and description; paths are relative to the mod folder.

Native-object notes use help.creatures.entries.<id>.description, or the artifacts, heroes, spells, skills and towns equivalents. See examples/object_notes.json.

Empty text is a JSON empty string. Save as UTF-8 or use Unicode escapes. UI labels and formats live under help.ui, help.text, help.sort, help.formats and catalogue facets.

categories.name: Objects and actions
categories.content:
Working examples uses an empty content string and overlay text for its explanation. This keeps a full-height article widget away from its controls.

objects is a consecutive array. kind accepts text, image, button, link and ErmFunction. value contains text or a resource name. Text without overlay: 1 joins the article. Fixed objects use x, y, width, height and zOrder relative to the content panel. Higher zOrder is created later. Leave gaps and stay inside the panel.

image uses a native PCX or group-zero DEF frame. It keeps its native size and must fit the rectangle. TwCrPort.def uses creature ID + 2; artifact.def uses the artifact ID.

Buttons and links run on left-button release. Actions: creatures:0, artifacts:7, heroes:0, spells:15, skills:2, towns:0, search and guide. Object actions open the same information card as a catalogue click, keeping the current page, filters and scroll position. mod:<folder>:<runtime category> opens an article. The return example uses mod:era help:1. Full http:// or https:// links open the system browser only when clicked.

ERM is optional. Install examples/HelpDialogExample.erm in the mod's Data/s folder, restart and start a map before using the optional category in examples/help_authoring.json. Its button calls HelpDialog_Example without arguments and shows a JSON-localized message. Other functions use erm:<name> or erm:<positive ID>. Opening or searching a category never executes actions.

categories.name: API and compatibility
categories.content:
Include headers/EraPluginsAPI/HelpDialogAPI.hpp in another plugin. ERAHelp_ShowDialog(page, subtype) opens the library; ERAHelp_ShowObject(page, id) reveals an object; ERAHelp_ShowObjectHint(page, id, popup) opens its card. Call after ERA initialization on the game UI thread.

Page IDs: Mods 100, Hotkeys 101, Creatures 102, Artifacts 103, Towns 104, Heroes 107, Secondary skills 108 and Spells 109. A popup hint uses RMB_Show and requires the right button to be held. Modal cards have a close button; creatures use their native window when a name and combat DEF are present. Invalid or unused IDs are rejected.

Creature and artifact counts come from the game. Fixed tables support 163 heroes, 28 skills, 9 towns and 81 spells. Additional scripted tables need explicit integration. Cards show current table values and defaults, not predicted combat results.

Documents use the canonical help.<folder> root. Missing translations display their JSON key, as returned by ERA; there are no substitute labels. Legacy categories.hotkeys.content accepts key or keys; a usable preferred hotkeys list wins. Contexts also accept numeric values -1 through 6 and the documented aliases.

Missing optional fields stay empty. Absent images and invalid DEF frames are skipped. Reading JSON and previewing search results never execute actions.

guide.content:
Browse
Choose a tab. Objects are sorted by ID. Left click an object for details; hold right click for a preview.

Filters
Categories are on the left; other filters are above the objects. Press a field or its arrow to select a value from the dropdown. Combine level buttons to show several levels. Reset clears filters and restores ID order.

Search
Type a title in the top Search field. Ctrl+F focuses it. Left click a result to go to and highlight it. Hold right click for a preview. Up/Down and Enter navigate too. Clear or Escape returns to browsing.

Hotkeys
Bindings are grouped by where they work.

7.description: Fortress combines swamp troops. Creature cards show defense, health, speed, costs and documented traits.

8.description: Conflux combines elemental troops. Multi-school spells can appear in more than one school category.
